extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent agents filing/ prosecuting patent applications in Singapore
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for requesting search, examination, supplementary examination and examination review reports in Singapore, including required forms, documents, timelines, fees, and format rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted request types and supporting reliance (Forms 10/11/12/12A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests may be filed as: (a) Request for search report (Patents Form 10) followed by request for examination report (Patents Form 12); (b) Request for search and examination report (Patents Form 11); (c) Request for examination report (Patents Form 12) by relying on: i. local search report issued by IPOS; ii. final results of a search of its application in suit during the international phase that has entered national phase in Singapore; or iii. final results of a search in one corresponding application, corresponding international application or related national phase application; (d) Request for supplementary examination report (Patents Form 12A) by relying on final results of any search and examination of its application in suit during international phase or final results of any search and examination of one corresponding application/corresponding international application/related national phase application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Rules 36, 37, 42, 42A, 45(3). See Annex for definitions/examples of corresponding application/corresponding international application/related national phase application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The search process involves a worldwide search for all materials and information which are relevant to the subject of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search is intended to identify relevant prior art. If application relates to two or more inventions not forming a single inventive concept, the examination/search may be restricted to the first invention specified in the claims and applicant will be notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination substantive criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination considers whether the invention qualifies as new, involves an inventive step and is capable of industrial application, among other requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During preparation of an examination report the Patent Examiner applies these substantive tests and may restrict examination for lack of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary examination grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: For supplementary examination, the Patent Examiner will only review the following grounds – support, relatedness of claims, morality, methods of medical treatment or diagnosis, double patenting, and no added matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 30 Oct 2017, the Examiner will also determine whether the invention defined in each claim constitutes an invention; if not patentable subject matter, Examiner will state full reasons in a written opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on supplementary examination eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may not request a supplementary examination report for: a) patent applications with date of filing on or after 1 Jan 2020; b) divisional applications with lodgement date on or after 1 Jan 2020.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change narrows the availability of supplementary examination to strengthen patent quality (see Section 29(11A) and Rule 43(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when relying on foreign search results / ISR
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant relies on foreign search results or ISR, a copy of the search results should be submitted. If not in English, a translated copy is required. All cited documents referred to in the search results are to be submitted by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation of non-English cited documents is not required at the point of filing the request for examination report, but the Patent Examiner may later request translations where necessary (see Rule 42).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrar-provided ISR exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Registrar had earlier sent a copy of the final results of the search or ISR in English to the applicant, the applicant does not have to provide copies of these documents when making a request for examination report on or after 26 May 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the applicant is still required to provide a copy of Non-Patent Literature cited in the search results to the Registrar as these documents have not been provided by the Registrar during the international phase (see Chapter 6.1.34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when relying on foreign final search/examination results, granted patent or IPRP
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant relies on foreign final search and examination results, a copy of the results and the list of allowed patent claims referred to in the final results should be submitted. If not in English, a translation of these documents with a Verification of English Translation (VET) is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance lists prescribed patent offices and the equivalent documents (e.g., Notice of Allowance, Decision to Grant) from those offices that qualify for reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for relying on foreign granted patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant relies on a foreign granted patent, a copy of the foreign granted patent and specification should be submitted. A declaration of download is required if downloaded from an online source. If not in English, a translation with VET is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sample declaration form is provided to confirm the applicant downloaded a valid copy which they wish to rely upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration on downloaded copy of a granted patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The declaration should indicate that the applicant declares the copy of the granted patent being submitted is a valid copy which the applicant wishes to rely on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample wording includes applicant name, patent number/application number, source, date and signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for relying on IPRP (Chapter I/II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant relies on International Preliminary Report on Patentability (IPRP) Chapter I or II, a copy of the report should be submitted. If not in English, a translation with VET is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same translation/VET expectation as other foreign results (see Chapter 6.1.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims correspondence table requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is required to submit a claims correspondence table setting out how each claim in the Singapore patent application is related to the claims in the corresponding application/corresponding international application/related national phase application, or the application in suit during its international phase. Each claim in the application in suit should be related to at least one claim in that corresponding application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must indicate the relation of the claims and explain how the claims are related to each other. Indicating only 'related' is not sufficiently informative. An example table and acceptable remarks (e.g., 'Identical', 'Identical, except ...') are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation that claims satisfy novelty / inventive step / industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: According to the foreign results relied upon, each claim in the application in suit should appear to satisfy the criteria of novelty, inventive step (or non-obviousness) and industrial applicability (or utility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the substantive assumption behind relying on foreign search/examination/grant results (see Section 29(1)(d)(iii) and Chapter 6.1.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary examination not acceptable for reliance on utility model results
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for supplementary examination report relying on utility model/patent applications are not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grounds for supplementary examination under Rule 46(1A) are limited because the corresponding patent application relied upon is assumed to have been examined and to appear to satisfy novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines for filing requests and abandonment consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms must be filed within their respective timelines shown in the table; otherwise the application will be treated as abandoned. For normal (non-divisional) applications, due dates are calculated from the declared priority date or, if none, the date of filing. For divisional applications, due dates are calculated from the actual date of filing of the divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table provides specific timelines (e.g., Search/Form10, Search & Examination/Form11 or Examination/Form12 deadlines such as 13, 36, 54 months depending on filing date). See Chapter 6.1.15 and Rule references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claim fees and discounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in excess of 20 at the point of filing the request for search and examination report (Patents Form 11) or request for examination report (Patents Form 12) are charged a fee per excess claim to encourage concise claim sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if 25 claims when filing Form11/12, 5 excess claims charged Prevailing Fee x 5. Additionally, a fee reduction applies where an ISR/IPRP established by IPOS exists for requests on or after 1 Apr 2017.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure prior to filing and grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention could be considered not new if made available to the public; such disclosure may be novelty-destroying. For applications filed on or after 30 Oct 2017, the grace period provision covers disclosures made within 12 months prior to the date of filing: a) disclosure by the inventor or person who obtained matter from the inventor; b) disclosure due to publication by an intellectual property administrator of an application for an IP right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may inform the Registry to disregard the disclosure as part of the state of the art by selecting the checkbox on Patents Forms 11, 12, 13A and 12B and attach a mandatory Statutory Declaration or Affidavit with supporting documents if any (see Chapters 6.1.18–6.1.24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory declaration contents for international exhibition disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: For international exhibitions, the Statutory Declaration should: a) state that the invention was exhibited at an international exhibition; b) state the opening date of the exhibition and, where first disclosure did not occur on opening date, the date of first disclosure; c) enclose one or more supporting documents identifying the invention displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are required to support a request to disregard exhibition disclosures under the grace period (Chapter 6.1.21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment requirements for erroneous publication
rubrics_metrics.description: For erroneous publication of application, an acknowledgment from an intellectual property office stating: a) the publication was erroneous; b) reason for erroneous publication; and c) the earliest date on which the application ought to have been published should be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to support disregarding erroneous publication disclosures (Chapter 6.1.22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal limitation of new grace period provision
rubrics_metrics.description: The new grace period provision only applies to disclosures made on or after 30 Oct 2017. Disclosures before that date will not be disregarded even if the patent application was filed after 30 Oct 2017.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should note the effective date when relying on the extended grace period (Chapter 6.1.23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to keep inventions confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite Singapore grace period provisions, individuals and businesses are strongly encouraged to keep inventions confidential until filing because not all jurisdictions have a broad grace period and third parties can still claim prior user rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is practical legal advice to preserve rights internationally (Chapter 6.1.24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities general checks on receipt of request
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a request (Forms 10/11/12/12A) is received, the Formalities officer will review requirements including: a) fee paid (if applicable); b) date of filing accorded; c) preliminary examination cleared; d) national security clearance issued if applicable (otherwise held in abeyance); e) application is not abandoned/withdrawn/refused/granted; f) representation details/address for service on the form correspond with record (otherwise file Form CM1 or CM2); g) there are no other pending related requests (specific forms listed); h) form is filed within timelines; i) for PCT national phase entry, amendments made in international phase considered and translations/VETs required if not in English; j) acceleration requests (ASPEC/PPH) handled per Chapter 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements are not met the form will be put on hold until related requests are processed or clarification requested (see Chapter 6.1.25 and following). The VET content expectations are listed (states document, verifies correspondence, translator details/signature/date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional checks for Request for Search & Examination (Patents Form 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Form 11, checks include: i) the number of claims indicated on the form should tally with the latest number of claims on record; ii) the 'ISR/IPRP established by IPOS' option is correctly indicated; iii) if applicant indicates a disclosure within 12 months prior to filing, the criteria and required documents (Chapters 6.1.18–6.1.24) are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are specific formalities to ensure correct fee, discount and grace period handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional checks for Request for Examination (Patents Form 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Form 12, additional checks include: i) all required documents referred to in Chapters 6.1.5–6.1.6 are submitted; ii) for divisional applications, a written notice/cover letter should be submitted if applicant intends to rely on a search report issued for the parent application; iii) for examination requests relying on foreign search results, the corresponding foreign application is valid and from a prescribed patent office; iv) number of claims indicated tallies with record; v) the option selected corresponds to the type of search results being relied upon; vi) if disclosure within 12 months is indicated, required documents meet Chapters 6.1.18–6.1.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 45(3) and related Chapters for details on acceptable foreign documents and prescribed offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional checks for Request for Supplementary Examination (Patents Form 12A)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Form 12A, checks include: i) application must be lodged on or after 14 Feb 2014; ii) application must have a date of filing before 1 Jan 2020 (divisional lodging date must be before 1 Jan 2020); iii) all required documents in Chapters 6.1.7–6.1.14 are submitted; iv) for examination requests relying on foreign search and examination results/granted patent/IPRP, the foreign application is a valid corresponding application or from prescribed patent offices; v) the option selected corresponds to the type of result being relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary examination eligibility is circumscribed and requires careful documentary support (see Rule 42A, Rule 46(1A)(b)(ii), Section 29(12)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification and correction procedures for form errors
rubrics_metrics.description: If form requirements are not met, the Formalities officer will send a letter inviting applicant to clarify/rectify within 2 months (or 1 month for some responses). To rectify errors, the applicant may file Form CM4 indicating the relevant rule (Rules 58 and/or 91) and select appropriate correction type (e.g., 'Correction of Form lodged', 'Correction of Specification', or 'Correction of any other document').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overpayment due to wrong selections will be automatically refunded after correction; underpayment requires correction and payment. If final search/examination result or granted patent/cited document is missing or wrong, extension of time is required to re-submit if the period to request supplementary exam has expired. Representation updates via CM1/CM2. Clarifications may be submitted via eCommunications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome when objections not resolved
rubrics_metrics.description: If the objections cannot be overcome or there is no response from the applicant, the request will be refused and the applicant will be notified via a letter. Applicant may request a refund of the fee paid for the relevant Patents Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal refusal procedures and refund processes are described (Chapter 6.1.27).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding to Patent Examiner upon compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: When the applicant has complied with the above requirements, the request will be forwarded to the Patent Examiner to conduct a Search, Examination or Supplementary Examination accordingly. The applicant will be notified and an entry will be made in the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More details on the examiner's procedures are in the Examination Guidelines for Patent Applications (Chapter 6.1.29).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for request for more documents during report preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: During preparation of the report/opinion, the Patent Examiner may request documents/information to facilitate/complete the report/opinion. The processing officer will request the applicant to submit the documents; if applicant does not respond within 2 months, a reminder will be issued; applicant may reply via eCommunications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely responses required to avoid delays (Chapters 6.1.30–6.1.31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of reports and handling of cited documents / Non-Patent Literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of search, examination or supplementary examination the Patent Examiner will prepare and forward the report/opinion to the Registry. If it appears that a matter has not been complied with, the Examiner will issue a written opinion as the first office action. A copy of each cited document will be forwarded to the Registry; if a cited document is Non-Patent Literature, it will not be provided due to copyright but details will be provided for the applicant to obtain a copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written opinions may be issued as first office action; NPL handling requires applicant to obtain copies themselves (Chapter 6.1.32–6.1.34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary search request requirements and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: If a search report indicates lack of unity (application relates to 2+ inventions), applicant may file Patents Form 10 for each invention within 2 months from the date of issuance of the search report by the Registrar. Upon receipt, the Formalities officer will review: a) fee paid; b) representation details match record; c) request filed within 2 months from search report issuance; d) 2 or more inventions indicated in the Search report/Written Opinion; e) applicant has indicated the group of invention intended for supplementary search request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements not met, officer will invite clarification within 2 months; applicant may file CM4 or Form 45 to extend time (Chapters 6.2.1–6.2.4). If requirements are met, request forwarded to Examiner and entry made in register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines for responding to Written Opinion or Invitation to Amend
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Written Opinion issued during examination the applicant may respond with written submission and/or amendments within 5 months from the date of invitation to respond. If an Invitation to Amend is issued, applicant may respond by submitting amendments or rejecting the invitation within 2 months from date of invitation. For Supplementary Examination, the period to respond to the written opinion is 3 months. These timelines are not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different timelines apply depending on type of action (search & examination/examination/supplementary) and are strict (Chapters 6.3.3–6.3.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for responses / Patents Form 13A
rubrics_metrics.description: A response to written opinion/invitation to amend must be submitted with Patents Form 13A. The response may include written submissions and/or an application to amend the specification with amendments indicated as per Chapter 5.1.12. From 1 Apr 2017, both marked-up amendments and clean copies are required for online submission. From 1 Dec 2019, if amendments/corrections have been made to claims, a marked-up copy and a clean copy of the full set of claims must be submitted. The request for amendment should set out reasons for amendments and any supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked-up and clean copies should be attached as correct document types; amendments must be based on latest specification on record. Failure to follow format may lead to disregarded responses (Chapters 6.3.10–6.3.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of late or improperly formatted responses; rejection of invitation to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: Any response not submitted within the timeline and/or submitted without the form will be disregarded. The invitation to amend may be rejected by the applicant via Patents Form 13A; when rejecting it is not mandatory to provide explanations, though applicant may do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late submissions are disregarded and can lead to Notices of Intention to Refuse (Chapters 6.3.8–6.3.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic system checks on response submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If all requirements are met or once the request is received, the system will automatically review requirements such as: a) date of filing on or after 1 Jul 2004 (otherwise use Patents Form 13); b) invitation to Respond to Written Opinion/Invitation to Amend has been issued; c) amendment and/or written submissions selected and filed; d) representation details match record; e) form filed within the applicable timeline (5, 3 or 2 months); f) ASPEC/PPH expedite indicated handled per Chapters 7.2/7.3; g) if disclosure within 12 months indicated, required documents meet Chapters 6.1.18–6.1.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System-level validation reduces clerical errors; applicants must ensure box ticks and attachments are consistent with facts (Chapter 6.3.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification process for response submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If any requirements are not met, the Formalities officer will send a letter inviting applicant to clarify/rectify within 1 month from date of letter (for response submissions). To rectify errors file Form CM4 indicating the relevant rule; to update representation use CM1/CM2; to submit clarifications reply via eCommunications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different correction categories to be selected when filing CM4 (e.g., 'Correction of Form lodged', 'Correction of Specification', 'Correction of any other document') (Chapter 6.3.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding response to Examiner upon acceptance; register entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Formalities officer will accept the Response to Written Opinion/ Invitation to Amend request and forward it to the Patent Examiner. The applicant will be notified and an entry will be made in the register that a response has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative acknowledgement and forwarding complete prosecution step (Chapter 6.3.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic Notice of Intention to Refuse when objections unresolved or no response
rubrics_metrics.description: If the objections cannot be overcome or there is no response from the applicant within the timeline following a written opinion, a Notice of Intention to Refuse will be issued automatically with the negative examination report. Similarly, if there is no response following an invitation to amend, the Examiner may issue a further written opinion or a negative examination report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System-generated notices and negative reports lead to the right to request examination review (see Chapters 6.3.15–6.3.16 and Rule 46(9)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Eligibility and Form 14 filing timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examination/supplementary examination report contains no objections or unresolved issues, a Notice of Eligibility will be issued. The applicant may request grant of the patent by filing Patents Form 14 within 2 months from the date of notification. If Form 14 is not filed within the timeline, the system will automatically abandon the patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file Form 14 leads to abandonment and an entry in the Register and Patents Journal (Section 29A(1)–(3), Rule 47(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Intention to Refuse and examination review timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examination/supplementary examination report contains unresolved objections, a Notice of Intention to Refuse will be issued with the report. The applicant may request an examination review report by filing Patents Form 12B within 2 months from the date of the notification. If Form 12B is not filed within the timeline, the system will automatically refuse the patent application at the end of 2 months and the refusal will be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status updated to 'Refused – EOT possible' on the register; applicant should timely file Form 12B to preserve review rights (Section 29A(4)(b), Rule 46A(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination review request requirements (Patents Form 12B)
rubrics_metrics.description: To request an examination review (Form 12B) the applicant must file within 2 months of the Notice of Intention to Refuse. The applicant may submit written submissions in response to the Examiner's opinion (mandatory) and/or amendments to specification (optional). From 30 Oct 2017, applicants may include proposed amendments with Form 12B instead of filing Patents Form 13 separately. From 1 Apr 2017 both marked-up and clean copies of amended sheets are required; from 1 Dec 2019, if claims amended, marked-up and clean copies of full set of claims must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request should set out reasons for amendments and include supporting evidence where appropriate; attachments must be of correct document type (Chapters 6.4.1–6.4.4).
